messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 4370012345 triggered: elevated 5xx rate on inference-hosting (eu-west). paging @oncall-alex :rotating_light:

oncall-alex: I’m on it, looking at dashboards now.

sre-jamie: seeing big autoscaler churn in eu-west: rapid node add/remove spikes starting 10:02 UTC. Pod crashloops on runtime-gpu pool.

eng-runtime-sara: logs show repeated CUDA OOMs inside the runtime: `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` around the same time as scale-ups. suspect rapid scaling + cold warmup of model caches.

infra-lee: k8s events show eviction then rapid re-scheduling, then OOMs again. autoscaler target went from 20 -> 70 -> 18 in ~6m.

oncall-alex: that explains token failures. customers hitting 502/504 and some model timeouts. support-maya, any customer reports?

support-maya: we have 3 high-sev tickets from enterprise customers in EU complaining about request timeouts and partial responses. CS is triaging.

eng-runtime-sara: paste logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T10:03:12Z] runtime: allocate kvcache 1.2GB
[2026-03-15T10:03:13Z] runtime:error: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY (alloc 1228800000)
[2026-03-15T10:03:13Z] pod: runtime-gpu-7f4b - OOMKill signal
```

sre-jamie: repro steps: sudden surge in queued requests triggers autoscaler, new nodes start but containers hit OOM while loading model segments; then kube kills pods and autoscaler interprets it as capacity pressure and keeps spinning up -> thrash.

oncall-alex: mitigation idea: 1) Pause autoscaler scale-ups (increase cluster-autoscaler max surge cooldown), 2) Force route new traffic to a validated fallback model variant (smaller quantized), 3) cordon some noisy nodes and roll runtime pods with reduced prefetch.

infra-lee: can do (1) now — setting scale-down/scale-up cooldown to 300s, disabling aggressive burst.

eng-runtime-sara: I can flip routing to model-quant-1 for eu-west at the router layer, fallback flag ON. That should reduce memory pressure per pod.

oncall-alex: do (1) and (2). attach runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/serving-autoscale-thrash

infra-lee: kube command I ran:
```bash
# temporarily limit cluster autoscaler burst
kubectl -n kube-system edit configmap cluster-autoscaler
# set --scale-down-unneeded-time=300s and --max-node-provision-time=10m
```

eng-runtime-sara: routing flip initiated — switching 50% of eu-west traffic to model-quant-1 and enabling kv-prefix cache warmup on remaining instances.

support-maya: notifying impacted accounts: rollback options, suggested mitigation (use dedicated capacity or pinned variant), CS sending templated update.

pm-jon: what's the ETA to restore <2min tail latencies?

sre-jamie: after cooldown + routing change we should see reduced churn in ~2-4m, full stabilization ~10-15m.

oncall-alex: observed immediate drop in pod restarts and node churn. 5xx rate down from 8% -> 1.6% in 3m. :thumbsup:

eng-runtime-sara: still seeing some pods with cached segments causing OOM on restart. starting a selective rolling restart of runtime-gpu pool with `GRACEFUL_PREFETCH=0` env to avoid prefetching large segments during boot.

infra-lee: cordoned 3 nodes showing repeated OOMs to prevent scheduler from placing new pods there.

eng-runtime-sara: command used for rolling restart:
```bash
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/runtime-gpu --selector=pool=eu-west --record
# set env GRACEFUL_PREFETCH=0 temporarily
```

oncall-alex: allocating temporary extra logging and tracing to capture cold-start memory footprint.

support-maya: customers updated: "We have degraded throughput in EU while we mitigate a memory pressure issue. Some requests may return 5xx; we are routing to a lower-memory model to reduce impact."

pm-jon: flagging this for postmortem — need clearer autoscaler safeguards and pre-warm policies.

sre-jamie: agree. immediate follow-ups: (A) re-evaluate autoscaler thresholds and burst logic, (B) add graceful warming/rolling lift, (C) add model variant automatic fallback when node OOM frequency crosses threshold.

eng-runtime-sara: also adding alert for rapid node add/remove (>10 in 5m) to prevent thrash loops.

oncall-alex: handing off to oncall-alex+1 for next shift. Summary for next oncall: incident 4370012345 — root cause autoscale-induced thrash with CUDA OOMs during model load. Mitigations applied: autoscaler cooldown, route 50%->quant variant, cordon noisy nodes, rolling restart with prefetch disabled. Customer impact: multiple EU enterprise timeouts, partial 5xx spikes; CS notified. Stability: stabilizing, monitoring.

eng-runtime-sara: leaving temp feature flags: `force_quant_fallback=eu-west` and `graceful_prefetch=0` until PRD review.

infra-lee: logs/metrics archived to incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/4370012345/ for postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident 4370012345 acknowledged and marked: mitigations in place. Next step: postmortem scheduled. :white_check_mark:
